headline: BULLISH
headline_tag: Recovery holds, but rising bond yields made this week shaky

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The longer-term picture is good enough to support spending more on bringing in new users, especially for products aimed at active traders rather than stablecoin savers. Because the 200-day average has not turned up yet and rising bond yields made this week shaky, scale up in steps rather than all at once, and keep part of the budget flexible so it can be pulled back if price falls back below its long-term averages. This describes today's conditions, not a forecast.

reasons: Price is about 17% above its 200-day average, so the recovery is still intact.
Up about 33% over 90 days, but only about half of those days closed above the long-term average.
The 200-day average still slopes slightly down (-3% over 90 days): early recovery, not confirmed.
Mood index at 71 (greed) while more traders than usual are betting on a fall.
watch: The bigger picture is positive, but US 30-year bond yields just hit their highest since 2002 and BTC dipped below $84,000 overnight. A daily close above $86,603 would ease that pressure; a close below $80,293 (the 50-day average) would weaken today's positive read.
analysis: Bottom line: the bigger recovery is still in place, but the next few days look shaky, so lean in step by step. Short term, the mood has cooled slightly to the negative side: the market's mood index still reads 71 (greed), yet more traders than usual are betting on a fall, and news is pulling it down a little after US 30-year bond yields topped 5.7%, the highest since 2002 (PANews), and BTC briefly slipped below $84,000 overnight. A daily close above $86,603 (the 30-day high) would turn the week clearly up, a close below $80,293 (the 50-day average) would turn it down, and in between it stays choppy. Calmer bond markets would strengthen this; another jump in yields would weaken it, and active traders are the group most likely to react.

Over the next month, the picture is clearly positive. Price is up about 33% over the last 90 days, though only about half of those days finished above the long-term average, so the climb has been uneven; a US regulator's move toward rules for crypto trading (CFTC, via PANews) is adding a little. There is room to climb if price gets back above $86,603 (the 90-day high), while the month's gains fade if it falls below $80,293 (the 50-day average). The Fed's next rate decision on 27 October is the date to plan campaign timing around.

Over three to six months, the direction is positive but not yet confirmed. Price is about 17% above its 200-day average, but that average still slopes slightly down and price is about a third below its all-time high; Russia licensing its first crypto exchanges, with Sberbank planning products in December (PANews), is a small long-run plus. The recovery stays intact while price holds above $71,732 (the 200-day average), with $66,470 (the 200-week average) as the next floor and $124,753 (the all-time high) as the far marker. It firms up once the 200-day average starts rising; until then steady brand spend fits better than splashy launches.

team_notes.marketing: Keep leaning into active-trader and non-stablecoin channels: price is still up about 33% over 90 days and the mood index sits at 71, so attention is there. Lead with steady recovery, trust and licensing rather than 'don't miss out' urgency, since only about half of recent days closed above the long-term average and the overnight dip below $84,000 showed how fast things swing. Keep stablecoin-first campaigns running as a cushion through the Fed decision on 27 October.

items.why: BTC slipped from about $85,500 to below $84,000 early on 7 October as sellers dominated and bets on a rise were forced to close, according to CryptoQuant's Axel Adler Jr. ETH fell below $2,600, and many mid-size altcoins dropped harder, around 8-11% in a day. The reports point to selling pressure, alongside US 30-year bond yields reaching their highest since 2002, rather than a single crypto event.
items.marketing_angle: A good day for content on handling price swings rather than promo pushes on smaller coins.

items.why: At TOKEN2049 in Singapore, Hyperliquid's founder said options will be the platform's next key product. Singapore's central bank said Hyperliquid, though headquartered there, is outside its regulatory reach. Its HYPE token fell with the market today but is still within about 9% of its all-time high.
items.marketing_angle: Competitor watch: on-chain trading venues keep adding products, a talking point for product and content teams.

items.theme: New exchange rules in the US and Russia
items.why: The US CFTC chair said that under proposed rules only federally regulated crypto exchanges could offer trading with borrowed money, and the agency is seeking input on a framework for crypto spot markets. Russia's central bank registered its first licensed crypto exchanges and custodians, with Sberbank planning crypto products in December.
items.marketing_angle: Licensing and regulation are a trust message worth leading with in regulated markets.

summary.short: Net negative: a jump in long-term US bond yields, a burst of forced selling and a day of fund outflows weighed on the near-term mood.
summary.medium: Mildly positive: a US regulator moved toward a crypto spot-market framework and a major bank backed OKX, partly offset by a Senate probe into USDT.
